launches.title: Omlet for VS Code — Get React component usage insights in VS Code
launches.tagline: Analyze how and where your React components (and their props) right inside your editor
launches.body:
**tl;dr** _We just launched a VS Code extension for React devs, providing component usage insights within VS Code — install it _[_here_](https://omlet.dev/extension)_ and ping us at _[_hi@omlet.dev_](mailto:hi@omlet.dev)_ with any feedback!_

---

---

---

Hey folks, Berk here from Zeplin (S15). 👋

Back in 2023, we launched our second product Omlet, a component analytics tool for React — and today, we're super excited to announce **Omlet for VS Code**. Our biggest update since!

# What is Omlet for VS Code?

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=88516&key=user_uploads/15544/f090d5bb-ec09-4c5b-ac34-4e4dc441e638)

Omlet for VS Code helps you **analyze how and where your React components (and their props) are used right inside your editor** — helping you confidently update, clean up, and maintain your component library.

Here’s a demo I just recorded: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BsZMMcHG3Ks>

If you want to learn more, read our full update here:

🔗 [Introducing Omlet for VS Code](https://omlet.dev/blog/omlet-for-vscode/)

# What do we need?

**We need feedback from React devs and design system teams.** We’d really appreciate it if you could [give the extension a try](https://omlet.dev/extension) yourself or share it with your team. Ping us at [hi@omlet.dev](mailto:hi@omlet.dev) and let us know what can do better. We're just getting started so any feedback would be super helpful.

Cheers!
